name: LP-MSPM0L2228 LaunchPad development kit
sources: MSPM0L222x data sheet SLASF94A (features); LaunchPad user guide SLAU928B (board parts, jumpers Table 2-1, LCD Table 2-3, Figure 4-2 header pinout); read from the chip 2026-11-09 (DEVICEID 0x1BB9F02F, SRAMFLASH 256 kB and 32 kB)

columns.head: The chip: MSPM0L2228
items: Processor: Arm Cortex-M0+
Runs the program, up to 32 million steps a second (32 MHz), from an internal oscillator or the 32 MHz crystal on the board
Flash: 256 kB, two banks
Holds the program. Two banks that can swap places, so a new program can be written while the old one runs
RAM: 32 kB
Working memory while it runs, with error correction
Backup memory: 32 bytes
Kept on the battery island when the main supply is gone
Power: 3.3 V on this board
The chip accepts 1.62 to 3.6 V; the battery island has its own pin

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: GPIO: 73 pins
Plain on/off pins: LEDs, buttons, control lines. 40 reach the board's headers
Segment LCD driver: up to 8 x 51 segments
Drives the glass on the board directly, no display chip needed
UART: 5 / I2C: 2 / SPI: 2
Serial text and sensor buses; two UARTs also speak LIN, IrDA, DALI and Manchester
ADC: 1, 12-bit, 1.68 Msps
Measures a voltage in 4,096 steps on up to 26 pins. No general-purpose DAC
Comparator with an 8-bit DAC
Compares a pin with a small reference it makes itself
Timers: 6, up to 18 PWM outputs
Timing and PWM for dimming LEDs and driving motors; one timer has dead-band for power stages
Security: AES, random numbers, CRC
Encrypts and checks data in hardware
Battery island: RTC, tamper pins, watchdog
Keeps time and watches two pins while the rest of the chip is off

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
USB debug probe with EnergyTrace, a 7-segment LCD, red LED, color LED, 2 buttons plus reset, 32 MHz and 32.768 kHz crystals, a 100 mF super capacitor
Not on the chip
No floating-point unit, no math accelerator, no CAN, no USB
In the box
The board, a micro-USB cable, a card
